beats.say: Orphaned at just ten: Johann Sebastian Bach lost both parents in just eight months.
His mother died in 1694 and his father followed eight months later in February 1695.
The ten year old moved to Ohrdruf to live with his eldest brother Johann Christoph.
By April 1700 he had begun studies at St Michael's School in Lüneburg.
He married his second cousin Maria Barbara in 1707; she died suddenly in 1720 while he was away with Prince Leopold.
He married Anna Magdalena Wilcke in 1721, and Felix Mendelssohn later sparked the Bach Revival with the St Matthew Passion in 1829.
Bach died in 1750 at 65 after complications from eye surgery, leaving a legacy revived by Mendelssohn.

facts: Johann Sebastian Bach was born on 21 March 1685 O.S.
He was the eighth and youngest child of Johann Ambrosius Bach and Maria Elisabeth née Lämmerhirt.
Bach's mother died in 1694 and his father died eight months later in February 1695.
The 10-year-old Bach moved in with his eldest brother, Johann Christoph Bach, in Ohrdruf.
By 3 April 1700 Bach had begun studies at St Michael's School in Lüneburg.
Bach married his second cousin, Maria Barbara Bach, in 1707.
Maria Barbara died suddenly on 7 July 1720 while Bach was in Carlsbad with Prince Leopold.
Bach married Anna Magdalena Wilcke on 3 December 1721.
Felix Mendelssohn precipitated the Bach Revival with a performance of the St. Matthew Passion in 1829.
Bach died due to complications following eye surgery in 1750 at the age of 65.
